experiments.scope: H1, H1-P1, H5' and the algorithm (proof.md Sections 2 to 5). Trials 0..4: a first block drawn from SHAKE-256 of the experiment id and trial seed, its real 38-step chaining value and a scan start u0 from the same stream, then the counted procedure of proof.md Section 3 at reduced size: the full 2^23-bucket table of 7-lane 256-bit words loaded with 2^17 candidates of the a0 set P (full scale: 2^27, so the buckets are sparse here and empty lanes give spurious matches, which the count test rejects), 2^11 distinct scan words u0 + n (full scale: 2^32), the SWAR test of both windows of every head, the straddle pass, post-filters C1, C2, G, F7 and step 3b on every good pair, every operation counted. Every claw is checked three ways: against an independent sorted search over the stored entries with multiplicity (reference_claws), by rebuilding the real E16 of member x and checking it is in S160 with W1 = u and a0 in P (bad_e16), and by evaluating the four post-filters on the real words of both members (bad_postfilters). A pair is returned only if step 3b accepts it (rows 16..21 pass and A34..A37, E34..E37 are equal), so a returned pair is a full collision; none is expected at this size. Trial 5 runs step 3b on the P8 semi-free-start pair itself. Trials 6..255 return no pair by design. A reduced-size fixture, not success-probability evidence.
experiments.hypothesis: Returned pairs: 0 (none expected at the reduced size; any returned pair would be a full collision). On every working trial (0..4): claws = reference_claws = distinct_pairs, bad_e16 = 0, bad_postfilters = 0; stored_lanes = 131072 (every candidate stored: the buckets are far from full); claws near 2^11 x 160 x 2^17 / 2^32 = 10; spurious_matches occur only on scan words with w = 0 or w in {507, 508, 511} (about 6 per 512 words, each with many empty lanes); counted_ops close to model_ops (the model mean at that size). Trial 5: s_pair_step3b_accepts = 1, s_pair_step3b_ops = 3014, s_pair_words_equal_pmx = 1. Our validation request (256 trials) ran in 12.3 s under --cpus 1 and 128 MB on a loaded host, with byte-identical output in two runs.

experiments.scope: Reproducible observations of the structure behind H2-P1 and H3-P1 (proof.md Sections 7 to 9); it does not test either premise. Trials 0..3: a seed-drawn chaining value, the claws of the procedure with 2^17 candidates in the full bucket table and 2^13 distinct scan words; for every claw both members are rebuilt from the real compressions and the tests of rows 16..21 of step 3b are applied in order, reporting how many claws pass rows 16, 17, ..., 21 cumulatively, how many are accepted (rows 16..21 and equal outputs), and the post-filter stage counts. A pair is returned only if a claw is accepted (a full collision); none is expected. Trials 4..255 return no pair by design.
experiments.hypothesis: Returned pairs: 0 (the acceptance probability of a claw is about 2^-87). On every working trial: row16 = claws (every claw is a row-16 pass of both members, Lemma 1 and the S160 check), row17 and beyond 0 at this size, accepted 0. Our validation request ran in 6.4 s under --cpus 1 and 128 MB, with byte-identical output in two runs.
